items.name: Lake Toya Sightseeing Cruise
description: Enjoy the beautiful seasonal scenery of Lake Toya from a sightseeing boat. You can also land on Nakajima Island for a nature walk or forest bathing.
From spring through autumn, special fireworks-viewing cruises operate to coincide with the Long-Run Fireworks Festival, offering a unique view from the water.

includedInPlans.name: Lake Toya Nakajima Island Cruise Plan

items.name: Lake Toya Long-Run Fireworks Festival
description: A signature fireworks festival held every night from spring to autumn. The lakeshore is just a short walk from the hotel, so you can casually enjoy an evening stroll and fireworks after dinner.

A rare festival nationwide, with fireworks launched over about 20 minutes while moving across the lake. You can enjoy it from a variety of vantage points — your room, the lakeshore, or a sightseeing boat — a special charm unique to Lake Toya.

items.name: Noboribetsu Marine Park Nixe
description: An aquarium modeled after a Danish castle, where you can get up close with sea creatures. A popular day-trip spot just a bit further from the hotel.
Highlights include the popular penguin parade, dolphin and sea lion shows, and a large tank. A great full-day outing for families, couples, and friends alike.

includedInPlans.name: Plan with Noboribetsu Marine Park Nixe admission ticket

items.name: Strolling Toyako Onsen Town
description: Just a short walk from the hotel, the onsen town is dotted with souvenir shops, cafes, restaurants, and foot baths. Enjoy a casual stroll unique to Lake Toya.
Take an evening walk along the lakeshore, or time your walk with the fireworks festival — the leisurely pace is one of the perks of staying overnight.

items.name: Illumination Tunnel
description: A popular winter spot that lights up Toyako Onsen town with a magical glow. Enjoy a leisurely evening stroll surrounded by colorful illuminations.
Perfect for a walk through the onsen town or an outing after dinner. It's also a popular spot for photos.

items.name: Lake Toya Canoe & SUP Experience
description: Enjoy a paddle across the clear waters of Lake Toya by canoe or SUP. The view from close to the water's surface has a charm all its own, different from a sightseeing boat.
Beginner-friendly guided plans are available, so first-timers can feel at ease. Experience Lake Toya's changing moods, from a quiet morning to a golden sunset.

items.name: Lake Toya Cherry Blossoms
description: In spring, cherry blossoms line the lakeshore and surrounding roads, creating a beautiful spring scene unique to Lake Toya. The combination of lake and cherry blossoms is a special view found only during this season.
A popular spot to enjoy Hokkaido in spring, whether strolling along the lakeshore or taking a scenic drive.
items.location: Around Toyako Onsen, Toyako-cho, Abuta-gun, Hokkaido

items.name: Bicycle Rental
description: With a rental bicycle, you can explore the Lake Toya lakeshore and onsen town at your own pace, easily reaching spots that are a bit far to walk to.
Cycling along the lakeshore breeze is a popular way to enjoy the changing scenery through the seasons — great for photography and café-hopping too.

items.name: Silo Observatory
description: A signature scenic spot with sweeping views of Lake Toya, Nakajima Island, Mt. Usu, and Showa-Shinzan. On clear days you can even see Mt. Yotei — a popular spot for travel photos.
The observatory serves its famous pudding and soft-serve ice cream, plus seasonal activities such as sky cruising in summer and snowmobiling in winter.

items.name: Mt. Usu Ropeway
description: A ropeway that takes you from the base of Showa-Shinzan to the summit in about 6 minutes. Enjoy sweeping views of Lake Toya, Showa-Shinzan, and even Funka Bay in the distance.
The summit has an observation deck and walking paths where you can experience up close the dynamic terrain shaped by Mt. Usu's volcanic activity — a popular spot with different views each season.

items.name: Showa-Shinzan
description: An active volcano born from a 1943 eruption that still shows its striking form today. Its reddish-brown slopes are overwhelming to see up close.
It's also near the Mt. Usu Ropeway and the bear ranch, making it easy to combine with other sightseeing. Feel the volcanic history and natural power unique to Lake Toya.

items.name: Lake Toya Sunflower Field
description: In summer, a field of blooming sunflowers vividly colors the blue sky and lake scenery. A sea of yellow flowers as far as the eye can see, and a popular spot for photos.
A seasonal spot offering scenery unique to summer. Also recommended alongside a drive or a walk along the lakeshore.

items.name: Volcano & Geopark Walk
description: At the Toya-Usu Geopark, you can walk trails such as the Nishiyama Crater Walk and the Konpirayama Crater Disaster Remains Walk, and see up close the traces of Mt. Usu's eruptions and the changing land.

Uplifted roads, craters, and damaged buildings offer a valuable look at the power of nature and the process of recovery. Combined with the Lake Toya Visitor Center, you can learn even more about volcanic history and disaster preparedness.
items.location: Around Toyako Onsen, Toyako-cho, Abuta-gun, Hokkaido

items.name: Showa-Shinzan Bear Ranch
description: Seeing brown bears up close is truly impressive. A popular spot to experience Hokkaido's great outdoors, offering an experience that captivates both adults and children.
During the feeding experience, the bears sometimes show off tricks hoping for a treat. If you're lucky, you may even meet an adorable bear cub for a memorable moment on your trip.

items.name: Lake Toya Ranch
description: Enjoy a horseback riding experience surrounded by Hokkaido's grand nature. Courses are available for first-timers to join with peace of mind.
A popular activity for spending relaxed time with the horses. Create special memories amid scenery that feels distinctly Hokkaido.

items.name: Lake Hill Farm
description: A popular spot where families and couples can spend relaxed time interacting with animals on a spacious farm, or playing with free-to-borrow balls and badminton sets. It's easy to lose track of time here.
Enjoy the farm's famous gelato, along with freshly baked pizza and local craft beer. A meal with Hokkaido's scenery makes the trip even richer.
